errors: "the library contains millions of different shapes": this understates the repertoire, which is commonly estimated at 10^8 to 10^10 distinct receptors per person.
"Across the body's hundreds of billions of lymphocytes": the usual estimate is about 10^12 lymphocytes, so this is low.
"The cause is a changed antigen, not memory cells that wear off.": this overstates the case for influenza, where waning antibody also lowers protection within and across seasons.

"Many have a better fit, because the clone mutates its receptors during expansion": this is applied to all lymphocytes, but only B cells undergo somatic hypermutation and affinity maturation; T cell receptors do not mutate.

why_best: D gives every link in the chain (random repertoire, selection, expansion, memory, race, and limits from antigen change) in the fewest words, with defined terms and a single comparison table, so this reader gets the full model with no detours.
